assumptions: HEURISTIC: a matched random sign-complete factor base approximates random-sum occupancy at these toy sizes.
UNTESTED: excess pair energy that persists with size may be compilable into cheaper recursive decomposition.
MODEL-BOUND: affine group and field-operation counters approximate this Python implementation only.
falsification_conditions: No coordinate family reaches the preregistered energy and five-term success thresholds at two of three sizes.
An apparent gain disappears after matching factor-base cardinality, sign symmetry, curve, targets, and operation accounting.
interpretation_limits: The 15-19 bit sweep cannot establish an asymptotic exponent.
Pair additive energy alone does not imply an efficient relation algorithm.
The experiment does not instantiate isogenous or alternative-coordinate model transforms.
A positive preflight signal is not a faster-than-rho ECDLP algorithm.
hypothesis.mechanism: A coordinate-defined set with non-random additive concentration may admit compressed two-sum and three-sum tables. Joining those tables can increase five-term decomposition success or reduce fixed-curve online work relative to a cardinality-matched random set.
hypothesis.statement: At least one tested coordinate-defined sign-complete factor base has persistent additive concentration and five-term target coverage beyond a matched random factor base without hiding more than a fourfold offline group-operation cost.

instances: one deterministic generated ordinary curve per bit size

parameters.factor_base_size: nearest even integer to q^(1/5), minimum 8
